headline: Second readings on a Transit Director order and a Customer Facility Charge order, plus closed-door legal talks on a KRT reassessment contract and Bangor Mall.
summary: The Transit Director order would set up a new department for the Community Connector bus system. The Customer Facility Charge order would pay for early planning of a consolidated rental car facility at Bangor International Airport.

MEMO 
To: City Council 
From: Courtney O’Donnell, Asst. City Manager 
CC: Carollynn Lear, City Manager 
Date: November 6, 2026 
RE: Transit Director 
The Community Connector is a regional public transportation system owned and operated by the City of 
Bangor and serves Bangor, Brewer, Hampden, Old Town, Veazie, Orono, and the University of Maine. 
Established in the late 1970s, it has become an essential part of the region’s community and economy. 
The system provides two primary services: fixed-route transportation and ADA paratransit services. 
In recent years, the Community Connector (CC) has made significant investments in modernization and 
service improvements, including transitioning to fixed stops, opening a downtown Transit Center, and 
implementing new technology such as a rider app, automated service announcements, and passenger 
counters. Current initiatives include rehabilitating the cold bus storage facility and adding training space, 
implementing a fare increase, partnering with Eastern Maine Community College to develop driver 
training solutions, and working with the Bangor Area Comprehensive Transportation System (BACTS) on 
a planning study to improve and streamline service. 
The system is supported by approximately 50 employees, most of whom are Transit Drivers. Like transit 
systems nationwide, the CC faces ongoing challenges recruiting and retaining qualified drivers. 
Contributing factors include more extensive commercial licensing requirements, legalization of 
recreational marijuana, and fewer affordable local training opportunities than in years past. The region’s 
size and location further limit the candidate pool, while school transportation providers represent a 
primary source of competition for qualified drivers. 
Our overarching workforce strategy is to create more attractive, sustainable career opportunities to 
improve recruitment and retention. This includes working with our local union, ATU #714, to transition 
drivers to full-time status. While this is a complex process, we believe it is an important long-term 
investment in workforce stability. Ultimately, our goal is to restore full service and maintain a stable 
driver workforce. 
Historically, the Community Connector has operated as a division of the City Manager’s Office, reporting 
to the Assistant City Manager. As part of an ongoing effort to strengthen the system’s organizational 
structure, we would like to hire a Transit Director. This position would provide dedicated, onsite 
leadership and specialized transit expertise while allowing the City Manager’s Office to redirect its 
capacity toward other municipal priorities. 
In addition to its operational responsibilities, the CC receives federal funding directly through the 
Federal Transit Administration (FTA), which carries substantial administrative, reporting, and regulatory 
compliance requirements. Given the complexity of these responsibilities, the system’s ongoing capital 
and service improvements, and the need for dedicated operational leadership, staff recommends 
establishing the Community Connector as its own City department, led by a Transit Director. 
Therefore, staff recommends that the City Council authorize the use of up to $65,000 from 
undesignated fund balance to support the Transit Director position for the remainder of the current 
fiscal year. Staff will work to minimize the amount drawn from fund balance to the extent possible.
Memorandum 
    
To: Council Workshop 
 
From: Jose F. Saavedra, Airport Director 
 
CC: Carollynn Lear, City Manager  
        
Re: Customer Facility Charge (CFC) Program and Consolidated Rental Car Facility 
(CONRAC)  
 
Date: November 9, 2026  
 
 
 
1. Background  
 
Bangor International Airport (BGR) currently accommodates five rental car companies operating 
from facilities located within and around the Airport terminal. As passenger traffic continues to 
grow, the Airport must evaluate its existing rental car infrastructure to ensure adequate capacity, 
operational efficiency, and a positive passenger experience. 
 
To address these needs, the Airport established a Customer Facility Charge (CFC) program 
earlier this year. A CFC is a fee collected from rental car customers that provides a dedicated 
funding mechanism for the planning, design, construction, and operation of rental car facilities. 
 
The Airport's long-term objective is to develop a Consolidated Rental Car Facility (ConRAC), 
bringing rental car operations into a more efficient and coordinated facility. This approach would 
allow the Airport to address existing infrastructure limitations while planning for future passenger 
growth and rental car demand. 
 
The ConRAC project is included in the Airport's Master Plan and five-year Capital Improvement 
Plan. 
 
 
2. Current Status and Next Steps 
 
With the CFC program established, the Airport is preparing to begin the initial planning and 
feasibility phase of the ConRAC project. 
 
This work will be performed by Mead & Hunt, the Airport's engineering consultant, under its 
existing five-year comprehensive airport engineering services contract. 
 
The initial planning effort will include: 
 
• Evaluating existing rental car operations, infrastructure, and future facility requirements.
• Reviewing potential locations and developing alternatives for a consolidated facility. 
• Conducting financial analyses to evaluate project feasibility and potential funding 
requirements. 
• Identifying near-term improvements to address existing capacity constraints. 
• Developing an environmental strategy and identifying the next steps necessary to 
advance the project. 
 
This initial phase is intended to provide the Airport with the information necessary to make 
informed decisions regarding the location, scope, financial feasibility, and future development of 
the facility. 
 
The results of this effort will help guide subsequent planning, design, and implementation 
decisions. Any future capital expenditures requiring Council authorization would be brought 
forward through the appropriate approval process. 
 
 
3. Action Before Council – November 9, 2026 
 
At its October 19, 2026 meeting, the Business and Economic Development Committee 
recommended approval of a $222,040 appropriation of Customer Facility Charge funds to 
support the initial ConRAC planning effort. 
 
The appropriation received its first reading before the City Council on October 26, 2026, and is 
scheduled for its second reading and consideration on November 9, 2026. 
 
Airport staff will be available during the Council workshop to provide additional background and 
answer any questions regarding the CFC program, the proposed ConRAC project, and the 
appropriation before Council.
